Industry observers note that shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

In a recent development, the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that mentioned it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

Sources indicate that the Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

In a recent development, shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Recent findings suggest that across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

Recent findings suggest that the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

In a recent development, the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

In a recent development, even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

According to recent reports, as a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

In a recent development, on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still reveals that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Planes are, without a doubt, the fastest way to get around the map in GTA VI. They can help you explore areas to find points of interest or simply get to a pinged location in a flash.

Industry observers note that however, finding a plane is easier said than done. In GTA VI, planes are typically found in very specific locations such as airports and airstrips.

Sources indicate that if you are looking for a sweet plane to take up into the skies, you have come to the right place. Here are the best places to get a plane in Grand Theft Auto VI.

Players can find an airstrip on the southeast side of the Grassrivers in Mariana County. This airstrip has a plane that’s easy to control, and there is usually no one around, making it easy to steal.

Industry observers note that in the northern section of Belville in Leonard County, you will find Lake Leonida. Next to one of the docks on the lake, you will find a plane that’s easy to steal because the open water acts as a runway and there aren’t many people around.

In a recent development, in Borrachero Sound, a very small area on the west side of Kelly County, you will find an airstrip that lies next to the water. You'll usually find more than one plane here, so you’ll have options to choose from.

In the Waning Sands region of Leonard County, you will find an airstrip just outside of Belville. Similar to the plane spot mentioned earlier, you will also find more than one plane at this airstrip.

Sources indicate that last, but certainly not least, one of the best places to find a plane is, of course, the Vice City International Airport. Known as VCIA, you can find this airport in the southwest section of Vice Dale County.

Sources indicate that keep in mind that VCIA has high security, so stealing a plane can be tricky. However, it is an airport, so it has the most planes available, making it one of the best places to find one.

Recent findings suggest that if you’d like to get a plane in a more natural way, that doesn’t involve stealing, you can find one during the McKittrick Farm side quest. To start this quest, examine the poster inside the Starlet Motel office (mandatory location in Chapter 2), and the location of the farm will be marked on your map.

Industry observers note that since you’ll be stealing the planes mentioned in this guide, it’s wise to learn how to avoid the cops when flying. Even though the places I mentioned here tend to have almost no one around, with the exception of VCIA, there’s still a possibility that someone will spot you stealing it or report the crime once they realize it's missing.

According to recent reports, the best way to avoid cops' detection when flying a plane is to fly at low altitude. Flying low makes it harder for cops to see you, as buildings, trees, and other structures will help block their line of sight.

You only really need to worry about this if the heat star level reaches 3 to 4, when police bring in the helicopters. Otherwise, you can easily lose cops by simply flying away due to how fast planes go in the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies.".

In a recent development, if it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers.".

Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote.".

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that to get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, which is the much easier way to get in. If you'd still rather unlock the safe the classic way, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

It has been revealed that the GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

In a recent development, by the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

Sources indicate that you'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

You'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Fortunately, there are some sticky bombs conveniently stashed in the next room, meaning it's the much safer option that heading out to the boatworks.

We previously believed this option required reaching one of the Chapter 3 GTA 6 missions, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation, but with the few explosives available in the bowling alley, you're golden. Keep the spares on you, and you can use them to get into other safes around Leonida, too.

The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of upcoming content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to upgrade the community on what to expect in 2026.
  • The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of upcoming content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to upgrade the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one patch on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s fresh blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

According to recent reports, in the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of problems should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the upcoming roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo concerns, and other crashes and freezing.

In a recent development, the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another key area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more concerns join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next patch will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

Industry News: 10 Game Boy Metroidvanias You Can Finish in Under 10 Hours

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games.
  • It has been revealed that very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania.
  • The Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games. They’re still great games, sometimes the best titles of a console generation, but back in the day they were more niche.

It has been revealed that very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania. One of the biggest draws of these games is that you could complete them pretty rapidly, especially when it came to the handheld consoles.

The Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet. This list encompasses the shortest Metroidvanias of the broader Game Boy generation that you could finish in under ten hours.

Sources indicate that starting off with a strange one that fits a bit more into a Metroidvania-like category, Wario Land 3 did incorporate a lot of aspects of Metroidvanias. Playing as the treasure-obsessed Wario, players would navigate various levels attempting to find all the treasure chests available.

In true Metroidvania fashion, players could return to older levels of the game with new abilities to uncover other secrets they couldn’t get to before. The game did manage to make a name for itself thanks to some innovative gameplay elements and its relatively quick run-through.

According to recent reports, now the Castlevania series is absolutely a true Metroidvania, and one of the more difficult by many people's standards. Playing as Nathan Graves, players will enter Dracula’s Castle in an attempt to rescue their mentor.

Sources indicate that while not part of the main continuity of Castlevania, the game gained a following thanks to the difficulty and use of the Dual Set-Up System. This system gave players the ability to create new combinations of attacks via a card-collecting system, for interesting results.

Many of the best Castlevania games incorporate some sort of gimmick to make them a bit more interesting, and Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is no exception. Fifty years before Simon Belmont took on Dracula, there was Juste Belmont and their journey through Dracula’s Castle.

It has been revealed that the main feature of the game was the two versions of Dracula’s Castle that saw players moving between the two to solve mysteries and unlock paths intertwined between them. That’s probably the reason the game is on the longer side compared to most of the other Metroidvanias of the time.

In a surprising twist, this Castlevania game is actually set in the future, in 2035. It also abandoned the Belmonts for a brand fresh protagonist, Soma Cruz, who would discover his strange ability after being drawn to the castle during an eclipse.

In a recent development, in keeping with the lore of the game, the major system here was called the Tactical Soul System, and it would allow Soma to gain new abilities based on the soul he collected. This drove the main idea behind the Metroidvania aspects of the game and granted some freedom in character builds that players enjoyed.

Whether you’ve heard of the series or seen something from it, almost everyone can recognize Shantae for one reason or another. The series introduced in 2002 with some great Metroidvania elements that gained a large following, making it fairly popular.

The game introduced players to the half-genie protagonist Shantae as she did battle against her arch-nemesis Risky Boots. The key feature of the game was that Shantae could dance to transform herself into animals to perform different tasks and movement challenges, accessing other areas.

According to recent reports, the first Metroid game on the list, but not the first to pioneer the series, Metroid Fusion was the fourth game in the series. It brought a different kind of focus to the series, with the game sticking more to narrative and suspense than previous installments.

Sources indicate that this proved to be a great idea as the game revolved around Samus Aran and the infamous SA-X, a duplicate made with an infected suit. It brought an air of suspense to the game that stuck with players despite how short the game was.

Unlike some of the other Metroid games, Metroid: Zero Mission sought to revision the original game for a more modern era. Zero Mission introduced a lot of quality-of-life features to make the age of the original game a bit more manageable.

The game took pieces from previous titles that it had learned from, incorporating more story and expanded content. While still short, Metroid: Zero Mission managed to set a new path for the Metroid series as a whole, and is still seen as one of its highlights.

The second game in the series, Metroid II: Return of Samus, is one of the most iconic of all. This title introduced a few of the most memorable features that would become staples of the series, like the Spider Ball.

According to recent reports, not only did the game introduce some fresh mechanics, but it also focused on a darker world and story for the Metroidvania. The game clearly helped to build a dedicated fanbase despite its shortness, as its influences can be seen even in the newer Metroid releases today.

According to recent reports, A Metroidvania before the genre was even established, TMNT III: Radical Rescue was arguably one of the first few Metroidvanias. It featured a story focused on rescuing the turtles from the claws of Shredder in a beat-em-up exploration-focused game.

Each of the four turtles had a special use that would unlock more of the map for you to explore, effectively making the game a great Metroidvania-style game. There’s certainly an argument to be made that it would go on to inspire features in the genre.

A controversial title that ended up being basically expelled from the series for narrative reasons. It was a bit different from other entries in the series, being a more stage-based game rather than focusing on traditional navigation.

According to recent reports, regardless of any of that, the game is the shortest Metroidvania from the Game Boy era, clocking in at around two hours total. While perhaps not the most important Metroidvania over the years, it certainly has its place in history and our hearts. What a little curio.

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds.".

According to recent reports, GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director notes it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just quickly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

In a recent development, hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

According to recent reports, the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

According to recent reports, aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's revision.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the fresh one over.

You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB reveals a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game.

In a recent development, in fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. That's the beauty of PC gaming for you: Steam sales and mods keep games like this chugging along years after they'd be considered cutting edge.

According to recent reports, GTA 5 holdouts might have a long road ahead of them though. GamesBeat reported last month that "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" stated GTA 6 will make its way to PC in the first three months of 2027. In the past, Rockstar held PC releases back for at least seven months (GTA 5 PC took a year and six months), so an early 2027 release would be unorthodox if the report is true.

In a recent development, GTA Online, or some kind of multiplayer mode, will hopefully come at some point and it would make some sense to drop it at the same time as a PC release, or at least that's what I tell myself at night. I've only played a few hours of the game and I'm already imagining the kinds of mods that will inevitably show up in the first week. Someone is going to make it so Jason can instantly gulp down his coffee for the stamina buff, I know it.

For now, PC players will just have to continue biding their time in GTA 5 and pray that Rockstar at the very least confirms a GTA 6 PC release date sooner rather than later.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that as another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening.
    • Industry observers note that the press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year.
    • Bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now.

    Industry observers note that as another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business intends, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation.".

    Industry observers note that the press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the tech giant. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

    Bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is currently in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

    Tech Report: 6 JRPGs That Got Snubbed at The Game Awards 2026

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As has already been publicly revealed, DualShockers is part of The Game Awards jury, so while I have some say in which games get nominated, I am just one voice among hundreds of journalists and many, many outlets.
    • With that in mind, I put together a list of JRPGs that got snubbed at The Game Awards 2026.
    • Sources indicate that it was a massive joy to see Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter earn a nomination for Best Role Playing Game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As has already been publicly revealed, DualShockers is part of The Game Awards jury, so while I have some say in which games get nominated, I am just one voice among hundreds of journalists and many, many outlets. And just because I sit on the jury doesn't mean I agree with every outcome. Speaking from personal experience, none of the games I nominated for Game of the Year made the cut, and fair enough, my ballot was mostly JRPGs.

    With that in mind, I put together a list of JRPGs that got snubbed at The Game Awards 2026. You will find titles overlooked entirely, with no nominations, alongside JRPGs that earned a spot in one category but deserved recognition in others. That isn't to say the nominees didn't earn their accolades, but as usual, JRPGs keep getting neglected at these events in favor of mainstream juggernauts that sometimes fall short of the sheer excellence found in B-side JRPGs.

    Sources indicate that it was a massive joy to see Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter earn a nomination for Best Role Playing Game. I recognize that landing a Game of the Year nod would have been a tall order, and that is completely okay. However, if there is one thing the entire Trails series excels at, it is total dedication to its story, character development, and overarching narrative. With that in mind, leaving it out of Best Narrative feels borderline criminal.

    The entire heart of Trails beats through its storytelling. 2nd Chapter picks up right where Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter left off, expanding across Liberl and the growing threats of Ouroboros while diving intimately into each party member's backstory. It's gripping and enthralling, and even though it can occasionally be a slow burn and a bit bloated, the narrative payoff is sensational. Across all the Trails games I have played (seven so far), the series has never once missed the mark on its climaxes and final chapters, a feat worthy of serious praise.

    One of the strangest choices at this year's TGAs was seeing Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave land in Best Role Playing Game, especially considering Fire Emblem Engage previously competed in Best Sim/Strategy. I heard compelling arguments from a friend suggesting that because the RPG elements in Fortune's Weave were pushed further into the spotlight, the jury may have deemed it a better fit for the RPG category. Still, I suspect it was simply an oversight.

    To me, it would have made far more sense for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave to compete in Best Sim/Strategy, since being a tactical strategy RPG is the franchise's entire identity. There are two major reasons for this: first, if it hadn't taken a slot in Best RPG, another deserving JRPG could have slipped in, such as the very next entry on this list. Second, looking at the current Best Sim/Strategy lineup might leave you scratching your head, since the nominees barely seem connected to one another. What do Pokémon Pokopia, Mewgenics, and Star Wars Zero Company actually have in common? Nothing, aside from sharing a TGA category.

    Sources indicate that following my train of thought about Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave ideally competing in Best Sim/Strategy instead of Best RPG, I could easily picture The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales sliding into that open RPG slot. I realize the title, The Adventures, might make it sound like a pure action-adventure game. Yet, Square Enix officially classifies it as an RPG, and gaming outlets generally follow suit.

    Square Enix crafted an action RPG utilizing the HD-2D visual style, and the result turned out wonderfully. While its review averages hovered around 78, which explains why it missed out on nominations, I firmly believe the game deserved far more love. It is colorful and whimsical, brimming with a nostalgic sense of adventure and an intriguing narrative spanning multiple timelines (even if it completely glosses over the classic paradoxes of time travel). Then again, maybe this is just me wanting to shine a brighter spotlight on HD-2D projects so Square Enix keeps investing in smaller original IPs.

    According to recent reports, look, I will be the first to admit that Brigandine Abyss is simply an okay game. It is solid, and I had plenty of fun clearing two campaigns, though I didn't get nearly as much mileage out of its replayability as I did with Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia. Still, since I already started ranting about the strategy genre above, I might as well throw more fuel onto a fire of my own making. Do we need a dedicated Strategy/Tactical category separated from Simulation games? Runersia. Still, since I already started ranting about the strategy genre above, I might as well add more fuel to the fire of my own making. Do we need a dedicated Strategy/Tactical category separated from Simulation games? Hard to say, though several tactical JRPGs could definitely benefit from the spotlight.

    According to recent reports, brigandine Abyss is nothing short of a miracle, truly. The original Brigandine debuted on the PS1 and remained completely obscure, even among hardcore enthusiasts. Against all odds, Happinet revived the dormant IP with The Legend of Runersia, which apparently performed well enough to greenlight another mainline follow-up: Brigandine Abyss. If The Game Awards ever introduces a category like Second Wind or Back From the Dead, Brigandine would easily earn a spot on the ballot.

    I know seeing two Trails games nominated in the same year would sound wild, especially since the franchise only recently began gaining wider global recognition thanks to its remakes, but Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter could run only because the modern mainline entries came first. Do you enjoy the seamless blend of real-time field action and command-based turn combat? That hybrid system was born in Trails through Daybreak and carried forward into every subsequent release.

    In a recent development, trails beyond the Horizon continues the overarching saga that began in Trails in the Sky, which makes it a baffling place to jump in if you haven't been following the story. That would be like starting The Lord of the Rings with The Return of the King. Nihon Falcom makes minimal effort to recap past events, yet largely assumes enthusiasts have played the earlier chapters (which is precisely why they are working so hard to remake older entries). Hopefully, in the coming years, we will see non-remake Trails entries breaking into major RPG categories as well.

    Honestly, it is well past time The Game Awards introduced a dedicated Best Remake/Remaster category, as in my experience, these projects are often judged unfairly by the jury when stacked directly against brand-new releases. Without diving too deep into that debate, if Dragon Quest VII Reimagined had been a brand-new original title rather than a remake, I am almost certain it would have landed a TGA nomination, particularly in Best RPG.

    Dragon Quest VII Reimagined was, well, thoughtfully reimagined for modern audiences. The original release was notoriously bloated, taking hours just to reach your very first combat encounter. While the remake trimmed away a few islands from the classic version, those cuts worked wonders for the pacing. Both combat and character progression were cleanly streamlined, and random encounters were ditched in favor of visible monsters roaming the map. Dragon Quest VII Reimagined is a phenomenal achievement that delights newcomers and longtime veterans alike.

    It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another fresh entry.

    Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

    The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

    That mentioned, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

    In a recent development, the gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet fresh characters.

    Industry observers note that speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

    According to recent reports, beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

    According to recent reports, the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

    Recent findings suggest that you can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, could Grand Theft Auto 6 come to Switch 2? That has been the massive question ever since Nintendo officially revealed its console last year, and it's something that we have mused over ever since (as unlikely as it may seem at an initial glance). Now that the game is out, the tech experts over at Digital Foundry have weighed in on the port possibility, and, perhaps unsurprisingly, they don't rate its chances.

    In the outlet's latest rundown, it touches on the "compromised" Xbox Series S performance. It isn't all that, with DF noting "frame-rates routinely lingering in the mid to high 20s during ordinary traversal and combat," but it's the system that regularly lands the most comparisons to Switch 2, so DF says that it would be "interesting" to see if it would be "possible for a further cut back version to ship on Nintendo's hybrid console".

    However, the experts point out that a Switch 2 port "feels extremely unlikely at this stage".

    "Unless there are massive changes made," DF's John Linneman states around the 53:24 mark in the above video, "I don't see how this could possibly work on Switch 2".

    The main reasoning seems to mostly come down to the sheer size of the damn thing. This is a game that is pushing even the highest-end consoles to their limit — "the huge CPU burden that restricts GTA 6 to 30fps on even PS5 Pro" — so how would the comparatively little guy Switch 2 ever stand a chance?

    Sources indicate that now, we're never willing to rule anything out completely. Switch 1 got its fair share of 'impossible ports' in its lifetime, and Switch 2 has already landed a handful of beefy boys that we previously never could have imagined making the jump intact. However, this one might be a step too far. Please do prove us wrong, Rockstar!

    Recent findings suggest that it's a shame, because by all accounts, the game is fantastic. Our sister sites Push Square and Pure Xbox both gave it 10/10 reviews, praising it as one of the greatest open worlds of all time. It shot right to the top of Metacritic's ratings, too, tying with Ocarina of Time as the best of the best.

    Do you think we'll one day see GTA 6 on Switch 2? Let us know in the comments.

    #97873. Tech Report: Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

    📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1053 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1053 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Tech giant of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge.
    • Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 patch's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.
    • In a recent development, the team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Tech giant of Heroes 3, and focus on problems players had flagged since launch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Tech giant of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

    Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 patch's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

    In a recent development, the team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Tech giant of Heroes 3, and focus on problems players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio.".

    Relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Organization of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of latest and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel says. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'.".

    Complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added new units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie notes. "It was a lot.".

    Recent findings suggest that as the 3.0 enhancement grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Company of Heroes 3, we were going to have an problem that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a fresh Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

    It has been revealed that not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Organization of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel says.

    Recent findings suggest that further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the significant 3.0 update release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Tech giant of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie says." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

    Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 patch that we had a big spike of consumers and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well.".

    "If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

    Industry observers note that the next release for Tech giant of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the patch, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding upcoming units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

    Sources indicate that after that, though, I ask if Relic plans to continue adding to Manufacturer of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a new project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing.".

    So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate….

    Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

    It has been revealed that these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

    According to recent reports, like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

    According to recent reports, assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a significant launch.

    Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

    #97870. 10 Hard to Beat Sega Genesis JRPGs

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1661 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    10 Hard to Beat Sega Genesis JRPGs

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • While many of us played our first JRPGs on PS1 or PS2, they existed way before then.
    • In a recent development, there's a good mix even with these JRPG adventures, which feature sword and sorcery fantasy, far flung future and others besides.
    • According to recent reports, as for how they're ranked, we dug deep to find critical reception, and did our best to sort these JRPGs accordingly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    While many of us played our first JRPGs on PS1 or PS2, they existed way before then. The catch was, many of the JRPGs on older systems were incredibly experimental games. They were less clearly defined, but still worthwhile. That especially applies for the Sega Genesis, which featured many hard to beat JRPGs.

    In a recent development, there's a good mix even with these JRPG adventures, which feature sword and sorcery fantasy, far flung future and others besides. No matter what, though, they all featured some capacity to upgrade your characters, and many were turn-based as well.

    According to recent reports, as for how they're ranked, we dug deep to find critical reception, and did our best to sort these JRPGs accordingly. So join me in my time machine as we head back to the glory days of the Sega Genesis with these hard to beat JRPGs!

    Industry observers note that while the Dungeons & Dragons series has come a long way, it's fascinating to see where it started, at least in videogames. And though Dungeons & Dragons: Warriors of the Eternal Sun was mechanically a pretty weird JRPG, it featured a pretty engaging plot.

    Sources indicate that it starts with typical warfare against lowly goblins, then has the human army warped to a mysterious land of the Eternal Sun. Meanwhile, something called the Burrower is driving all your allies insane. It's surprisingly Lovecraftian, and quite neat, especially from back in the Sega Genesis era.

    This JRPG has a lot of understandable dungeon crawler energy, with players mustering a party of four different characters whose race and class determines everything. And like any good JRPG, as you level up, you'll learn powerful new skills, though much is decided by the RNG roll of a dice.

    Even though I'm not a huge fan of the whole Mystery Dungeon craze, I can see the general appeal. I discovered them with the Pokemon offshoots, but they started way sooner. One of the first examples is simply called Fatal Labyrinth.

    Industry observers note that it's about chasing a vicious dragon that guards a Holy Goblet, and safely navigating 30 floors of dangers to get there. Enemies don't move or act until you do, so there's inherent strategy in Fatal Labyrinth. More unique, you'll do well to discover whether scrolls and potions hurt or harm you, and using them accordingly.

    Industry observers note that perhaps the most charmingly old school aspect of the game is that gold only serves one purpose – blinging out your funeral when you die! So make sure to stock up on vital food and powerful gear, and maybe your journey won't have an ignominious end.

    In a way, The Immortal makes a better novel than a videogame. It's the tale of a call from deep within a labyrinth from the wizard Mordamir. You're not the person he called, named Dunric, but you'll do! Along the way, you'll navigate through several levels, ride magic carpets, and discover the true nightmare of what happened.

    Like any good JRPG, there's NPCs here, and you can even cast magic spells to roast your enemies. Those include the likes of goblins, flesh-eating slimes, shades and even a diabolical dragon. Also surprising for the era, The Immortal was surprisingly graphic and violent at times.

    While the game features lots of fun fantasy elements, it's also painfully linear, which made some feel it didn't do enough for the genre. Still, a good early attempt, and one that experimented in some meaningful ways.

    I think it's fair to say that The Lord of the Rings inspired Sword of Vermilion on the Sega Genesis. The game features King Tsarkon, who is warped by a magical ring, and twisted to evil ends. A valiant knight named Blade saves the good king's child, and then 18 years later, counsels the prince on his deathbed. It's up to him to honor his dead father and his valiant protector.

    Industry observers note that as for how Sword of Vermilion actually plays, it has a lot of ARPG mechanics. Furthermore, the gameplay shifts depending on a variety of circumstances, and alternates between top down and side views for the exploration and boss battles.

    In a recent development, while the game has a lot of fun arcade energy, the graphics weren't seen as a high point, even back when it first released. On the plus side, it was also a console exclusive, meaning only those who owned a Sega Genesis experienced this classic JRPG.

    In a recent development, I'm usually a fan of when developers try something new. But with Phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom, it was actually a brand new team brought in who hadn't worked on the previous two games. On the plus side, they tried new features like branching narrative paths and multiple endings. On the negative, in some ways this didn't feel like a Phantasy Star adventure.

    In a recent development, phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom actually spans multiple generations, meaning you'll play as the descendants of your starting main character, which honestly feels a bit like Fire Emblem. Depending on who you marry, you'll continue the game with different abilities as various children.

    It has been revealed that this adventure downplays the Technique system, but it makes up for it with auto-battle and an icon-based menu. Either way, this is traditional turn-based fare that, at least for me, makes me feel right at home in any JRPG adventure.

    Recent findings suggest that unlike the last game, Ys III: Wanderers From Ys is very much a direct follow up to the previous Ys adventures. It features Adol Christin, mysterious statues and the advent of a brutal demon named Galbalan. The game also handles stats, equipment and experience the same as the other games.

    Recent findings suggest that where Ys III: Wanderers From Ys stands apart is that it utilizes a side-scrolling view instead of the more traditional top-down style. Also, you can't just auto attack anymore, and instead need to pres a button to have Adol swing his blade or cast spells.

    Sources indicate that while the game can be a bit grindy and repetitive, those who were already fans of the Ys series were very happy with this adventure. It could have done more to branch out, perhaps, but sometimes if it's not broken, you don't need to fix anything.

    Whenever you hear that Treasure developed a game, you have to pay attention. They make some of the most creative games out there, though usually it's more platformers than JRPGs. In fairness, Light Crusader is a bit of an odd duck, combining the JRPG genre with isometric graphics and action adventure mechanics.

    In a recent development, you play Sir David, who is trying to save the kidnapped citizens of Green Row. He can run and jump, swing his blade and generally beat up monsters. But he's also capable of casting elemental magic. They can be cast individually or combined, buffing David or healing him, amongst other uses.

    Along the way, you'll discover the entire game is about the slighted advances of a diabolical wizard. He wanted desperately to marry the Queen of Green Row, and in his petulance, eventually summons a demon. Definitely a quirky adventure, but a memorable one, even years and years later.

    It took me a long while to get to Langrisser, a tactical series as popular in some spheres as Fire Emblem or Tactics Ogre. It didn't start with that name, though. Originally, it was called Warsong, and it was a pretty massive deal on the Sega Genesis. It's a fun but pretty brutal tactical JRPG adventure.

    In a recent development, like many brutal games, Warsong features permadeath, meaning if you're not careful, you could lose some of your best characters forever. Your commanders determine what units you can bring into battle, such as powerful Griffons.

    Ultimately, careful strategy rewards you with powerful upgrades to your commanders, including changing their classes. If all that wasn't enough, Warsong also features great music composed by Noriyuki Iwadare. A great game if you're strong enough to get through it relatively unscathed.

    There aren't all that many times I get really jealous about console exclusivity these days. But one of those classics I wish I had played back in the day was Shining Force II. It wasn't just good, but it was considered one of the best tactical JRPGs of all time.

    Some of the reasons people felt that way was due to how open-ended the game was, as well as the great visual flair. It alternated between top-down while exploring, and side scrolling during combat. Either way, the game was challenging, and forced you to lead Bowie and friends carefully.

    As for the plot, Shining Force II takes place 55 years after Shining Force Gaiden: Final Conflict, and is about Zeon's mayhem. But even if you didn't play the previous games, this is one tactical adventure that holds up, though it's also far from an easy time.

    It has been revealed that one of the more iconic games I played back in the day was Alundra. It was sort of like Zelda, but not really, and it really captivated me. One game that came before it was called Landstalker, a game about a treasure hunter named Nigel.

    Industry observers note that while Landstalker may not seem like a JRPG at first, there are a couple of reasons it qualifies as one. Even though you don't level up by traditional means, you can take on sidequests to improve your stats. There's also ways to improve your health, and even equip more powerful gear. A lot of it just requires a desire to explore as much as possible.

    Much of the game's overall challenge comes from devious death traps and gnarly puzzles, not to mention challenging boss battles. Definitely a strange old-school JRPG, but one that managed to delight fans by taking plenty of creative risks.

    Nintendo reinstates SmileBasic 4 to the eShop after it was used for Switch 2 jailbreaks

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (457 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop.
    • Industry observers note that smileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing owners to code their own simple programs and games.
    • Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

    Industry observers note that smileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing owners to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

    Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow users to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

    Nonetheless, Nintendo acted promptly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to enhancement the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

    Recent findings suggest that even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a newly introduced update post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

    The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a fresh in-game currency to pay for them

    📅 04 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
    • Sources indicate that the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
    • The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis declared The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

    Sources indicate that the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

    The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

    In a recent development, created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

    Industry observers note that alongside this, the game is also introducing a newly introduced virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

    It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

    In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

    It has been revealed that in the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis mentioned that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

    In a recent development, you can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

    Latest Update: Nvidia shareholders have filed a lawsuit against the tech firm over claims that they were misled regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
    • According to recent reports, the suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm.

    If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

    According to recent reports, the suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Manufacturer’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly rapidly.

    In a recent development, as it at the moment stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

    The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre organization who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ubisoft has confirmed that it is laying off a total of 166 members of staff from its Canadian offices.
    • It has been revealed that the teams affected, Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec, are arguably two of the most prominent studios in the corporation.
    • The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ubisoft has confirmed that it is laying off a total of 166 members of staff from its Canadian offices.

    It has been revealed that the teams affected, Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec, are arguably two of the most prominent studios in the corporation. The former has been responsible for some of the most well-regarded entries in the Assassin's Creed series along with key entries in the Far Cry franchise.

    The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.

    GamesIndustry.biz states that the layoffs account for less than 4% of the total workforce at the studios, and that the employees affected were working on projects that had either been cancelled or significantly changed.

    Here's the statement provided by Ubisoft:.

    Recent findings suggest that "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations. As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

    "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

    Ubisoft's next major release is Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 classic Rayman Legends, developed in collaboration by Ubisoft Milan and Montpellier.

    What do you make of this latest round of layoffs from Ubisoft? Share a comment in the usual place and let us know.
