    8 Most Unhinged NPC Inner Truths From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit.
    • Well, it reveals the inner thoughts of the game’s various NPCs.
    • Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit. He gave you a few masks, you made a few sales, and you have received the Mask of Truth in return.

    What does this mask do? Well, it reveals the inner thoughts of the game’s various NPCs. I am not sure if you have paid attention to Nintendo games recently, but they have been adding in some interesting NPC dialogue.

    Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.

    If you walk around the town square in Castle Town, you can find some rather colorful NPCs, but one of the most unassuming of them is the old woman who stares at the fountain. She seems so sweet, but she is actually a thief.

    Listening to her inner thoughts, you see that they say, “The quality of the items people are losing has really gone downhill recently… Is that a recession indicator?”.

    This hits a little close to home considering many have questioned if the U.S. is entering a recession. Along with this, it is obvious that she is taking some of the goods that people have lost and keeping them for herself.

    Industry observers note that if you continue your search around the fountain in Castle Town, you can find a young couple who are dancing. While they seem rather sweet, their inner thoughts tell a completely different story.

    According to recent reports, when you read the thoughts of the woman, it will say that she hopes that the man doesn’t break her heart. It is a sad thought to be had because she is clearly worried about her future.

    Industry observers note that when you read the man’s thoughts, you see they say, “Wait… What was this one’s name again?” Clearly, this isn’t his only crush, and he is stringing this poor woman along so he has someone to dance with. Yes… dance with.

    In a recent development, some of the guards around Castle Town aren’t very excited about their job. In fact, some of them find it boring doing patrols all the time. One guard in particular thinks about it pretty frequently.

    When interacting with the guard in the room with the pots, his inner truth will say, “Guards… Soldiers… Heroes… It’s their fault there’s so much peace around here. Hm… What if I…”.

    In a recent development, the thought trails off after that, but you can clearly tell what he is thinking about. The man wants some chaos, and he is clearing thinking about being the cause of said chaos if something doesn’t happen soon.

    You may have seen the bearded man wandering around Castle Town in the past and Kakariko Village in the future. His beard is magnificent, and he will definitely tell you about it. However, he is secretly questioning its cleanliness.

    When you listen to his inner thoughts, they say, “I wonder if it’s true that beards are about as dirty as toilets…” For someone with such a massive beard, he shouldn’t be thinking that he is dirty, unless he wants to shave it off.

    This is a massive contrast to what he will tell you when you speak to him, as he will typically say that he has a fantastic beard, and will even offer to locate Ganondorf.

    Industry observers note that shiro is one of the many NPCs you can find around Kakariko Village, and you also help him out by rescuing him from the Gerudo as an adult. Well, he isn’t the happiest carpenter around. In fact, he is rather depressed.

    According to recent reports, his inner thoughts read, “How does one escape their own dreary life? ‘Cause I can’t do this forever.” Granted, he didn’t seem the happiest when I rescued him from the Gerudo, but I never would have guessed that he was this depressed.

    Looking into his thoughts, he seems like he could use some therapy because it sounds like he has been hanging around Lumiose City in Pokémon Legends: Z-A for too long.

    There’s a pair of laughing men who appear in Castle Town and Kakariko. No matter what is happening, the pair consistently laugh at one another. They typically talk about stories they find funny, with the one laughing at the other for getting caught sneaking into the castle or falling off a horse.

    However, when you read their inner thoughts, the one states, “It’s exhausting wearing this forced smile all the time.” The other one will remark about how he knows his friend’s smile is fake.

    It’s sad that they continue to laugh constantly. Maybe they should just try to chill out for once and give up on the laughter. Are they cursed? Maybe they are cursed.

    According to recent reports, if you have explored Kakariko Village, you are for sure aware of the cucco lady. All of her cuccos get out of the pen, and you must go rescue them for a reward. In the future, she is living with a questionable character.

    If you use the Mask of Truth while you are an adult, you will catch her inner thoughts. They say, “That guy who lives with me always makes the most intense eye contact. He must really love cuccos…”.

    It has been revealed that what she is describing does not sound healthy at all. In fact, it sounds almost like something bad is going to happen and she is just waiting for the inevitable. Maybe she should choose a different place to live or kick the guy out.

    There is an old man who likes to wander around Castle Town. He will go in and out of shops, but mostly he will walk around the fountain. Just be careful listening to his thoughts because he has a particular woman on his mind.

    His inner thoughts read, “This kid… The mask’s neat and all, but I’m more interested in finding a particular damsel…” While it doesn’t seem so bad at first, if you talk to him, you can piece things together.

    It has been revealed that talking to him, he will make remarks about how he is looking for a lady who can make a potion, and will gawk at how beautiful she is. He will also casually talk about how we are at the age to be thinking about that.

    Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled.
    • The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation.
    • Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, upcoming reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

    The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

    Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Newly introduced Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

    According to recent reports, however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Newly introduced Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

    Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

    Sources indicate that furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

    Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

    This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-latest globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

    Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no confirmed platforms.

    Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

    [Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Queen's Domain has, by my count, four categories of collectible you have to hoover up if you want to see its more hidden endings, and some of them are real bastards to find⁠—I'd resigned myself to queueing up guides on YouTube to get it all done.

    In a recent development, guides are great, you might still need them for some of the collectibles, and if there's one game that feels like it was designed with Google/Reddit/forum help in mind, it's Queen's Domain. But I was thrilled to discover that, very late in the game, Queen's Domain provides a waypoint tool to guide you to its hidden collectibles. It turned what I worried would be a tedious process into yet another example of this game's boundless capacity for surprise and discovery.

    Recent findings suggest that I know I would have appreciated the heads-up, the permission to not worry about finding them all earlier in my playtime. If that's how you felt, and you aren't looking for spoilers, great: You can stop reading here. Granted, the spoilers in Queen's Domain are so absurd and out there as to be incomprehensible to someone early on in a playthrough.

    Sources indicate that there are two requirements to get homing compass guidance in Queen's Domain: You need a fully kitted-out Mask of Second Sight, and to discover the hidden Petrified Garden zone. You can technically reach the latter from very early in the game, but you won't be able to open the necessary path until you acquire all of the lenses for the mask. Here's a quick checklist:.

    That's basically, like, the entire third act of the game and encompasses most of the requirements for Queen's Domain's second of four endings⁠—this is super lategame stuff.

    Industry observers note that you can reach the Petrified Garden by jumping off the teleporter platform while you're in the spacey void warping between zones. The large platform to the side you can dash to is a boss arena⁠—kill the familiar-looking guy here to reawaken the very high-level enemies in the garden.

    Recent findings suggest that from there, you can find four god seals scattered through the zone with the Mask of Second Sight. Breaking them all opens a trap door to a secret area below the garden. At the end of the path, you can talk to a mysterious entity behind a sealed gate who spells out the criteria for unlocking endings three and four: Finding all mementos and silver-etched skulls in the game.

    Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

    Recent findings suggest that they'll also, helpfully, provide a final duck to unlock new items at Umbada's shop. Among this last tranche of material, Umbada will now sell six charms that attach to the Mask of Second Sight. These charms reveal the locations of silver skulls, unopened treasure chests, treasure lizards, Gagi meals, data modules, and Orbewa eggs.

    The respective tchotchkes appear as little holographic waypoints onscreen when you're within a few dozen meters of them and wearing the Mask of Second Sight. It can still take some sleuthing to reach the general proximity for these waypoints to appear, and there were some tricky placements that required me to think things through or circumnavigate the level and approach the waypoint from a different direction. But generally, the mask charms changed this collectathon portion of Queen's Domain into another fun part of the experience, rather than a completionist chore.

    Sources indicate that firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry.

    Xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.

Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few latest weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

    Tech Report: Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

    📅 06 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The significant Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods.
    • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
    • In a recent development, season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The significant Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

    You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

    In a recent development, season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

    In a recent development, patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

    When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

    In a recent development, starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the latest Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

    If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

    Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

    It has been revealed that the Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

    Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

    There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

    The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

    Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

    Industry observers note that the trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

    The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

    Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

    The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

    Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

    Infinity Nikki is making headlines with its latest controversy about including Maye Musk in their 3.0 introductory trailer for Chinese players, but it seems that there are actually great surprises, according to other livestreams.

    Today, in the main dev livestream for Chinese players (translated by YouTuber Whimsy Haven in English), which is where most things are revealed before the patch actually drops.

    In the Infinity Nikki universe, people are coming up with theories and release schedules, where we are all travelling to next, and what the next abilities are.

    With Grand Theft Auto 6 grabbing everyone’s attention, it seems like a genius nod that the cosy styling game decided to show its claws and add guns to the mix.

    Nikki, in all her infinite universes and extended lore, is no stranger to guns, but so far it has been discussed heavily by fans whether Infold would take a safer approach and not give Nikki guns in the latest game.

    It has been revealed that thankfully for all lovers of shooters, that is not the case. Nikki already has a huge backdrop of dark lore, and it only makes sense that they would dim the vibes in-game even further with the addition of guns to use against foes and Esselings.

    The addition of a pink Barbie-esque convertible makes the Grand Theft Auto comparisons even funnier for fans of both, as we are all consumed by the hype for the Rockstar instant classic.

    Unlike Rockstar, Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of her dancing with a upcoming character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles. Some fans are taking it as a further nod to the queer fans and those locked into Nikki lore, where rumours of her sexuality have floated from the early games.

    Industry observers note that but of course, the main star of the show is Nikki and the newly introduced character using guns. Now, with her new 'gal pal,' you can switch guns on the go as you fight foes, from a semi-automatic pistol to a short-barreled shotgun, as shown in the livestream.

    This is not the first gun in Infinity Nikki, as in 2.4 Nikki had a hunting shotgun which would only show up when the ability was used and wasn’t as flexible, leaving many fans disappointed but hopeful for more guns further on.

    Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of dancing with a new character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles.

    The other upcoming weapons seem to be wizard staffs, as we have already had a few wands in accessories rather than actual weapons, which makes sense in a game with a heavy dress-up mechanic.

    In a recent development, the controversy with Maye Musk, Elon Musk’s mother, certainly put a dent in Infinity Nikki’s reputation, and the conversation between fans and devs has been strained. Nikki and her games are no strangers to controversy, and with the latest fiasco with Love and Deep Space still ongoing about Valko, only time will tell how Infold will react to all the communication between them and fans.

    Infold has generally been receptive to Infinity Nikki fans, who have been asking for guns, darker storylines, more romance (even if only hinted at), among other things.

    Sadly, we’re not sure if you can do drive-by shooting Grand Theft Auto style yet, as the footage of the car mostly focused on the streets of Cicia, but knowing Nikki and how you can summon the unicorn, bike, or motorcycle in different areas, the car should be able to breeze through weird forest terrain.

    It may make sense to ask for drive-by shooting mechanics in the next questionnaires for more fun updates, as the devs do listen to what the fans want to see next.

    All in all, interesting things are happening in the next major Infinity Nikki update! No mention of poor Giovanni, though; he’s still in the basement.

    Infinity Nikki is available on PC, macOS, PlayStation 5, and iOS and Android phones.

    Industry observers note that it's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain firm finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.

    IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business concerns they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

    In a recent development, zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he stated.

    Sources indicate that it was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

    Industry observers note that essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Patch, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
    • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
    • In a recent development, since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Patch, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

    The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

    In a recent development, since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Enhancement to actually see it in action.

    Industry observers note that the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

    In a recent development, the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

    It has been revealed that the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

    Industry observers note that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

    Warlocks arrive alongside upcoming Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

    Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the substantial day.

    #97848. 10 Best Metroidvania Boss Fights of the 2020s (So Far)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1630 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    10 Best Metroidvania Boss Fights of the 2020s (So Far)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.
    • I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.
    • With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.

    I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.

    With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.

    Therefore, if you're like me and fascinated by a good duel with health bars and numerous phases, I invite you to read this list of the ten best Metroidvania boss fights of the 2020s (so far).

    Well Dweller is a magnificent video game that, as the pinnacle of Kyle Thompson's craft, is brimming with spectacular yet accessible special bosses, such as The Queen.

    The plethora of sequences, attacks, and projectiles that unfold during your final encounter is breathtaking, truly connecting with the idea that royalty rules with an iron fist because they actually possess the power to dominate others.

    Disfiguring the face of your family's kidnapper is fitting for a title that's cozy on the surface but profoundly dark beneath it, materialized in a demanding fight in terms of positioning and movement that makes you feel like you're constantly swimming against the tide.

    While the bosses in Well Dweller wouldn't be my primary reason for recommending this gem, The Queen, in particular, demonstrates the wide variety that Metroidvanias can offer, rather than simply reducing everything to dodging and attacking in between.

    The entirety of Shinobi: Art of Vengeance is a moving marvel with choreography worthy of the best action sequences of recent years, thanks to the tremendous animations and magnificent display of audiovisual effects for bosses like Lord Ruse.

    Its imposing arena and visual design provide the perfect backdrop to prepare you for the epic duel this tormented villain has in store, whose tragic origin story is only surpassed by the way his darkness permeates the fight.

    What was once an honorable man surrenders his body and mind to an abject power that threatens the balance of the world, making it fitting that his fight resembles that of a ninja against a natural phenomenon capable of defying the laws of physics.

    The gameplay is very satisfying, forcing you to use all the tools and combos at your disposal to evade and attack effectively, leveraging the title's glorious combat system, where, after dominating all the combos, you can truly perform a martial aesthetic feast.

    The gimmick of having you constantly face a boss throughout a game is quite difficult to pull off successfully, but Gilroy, the Administrator from Ender Magnolia: Bloom in the Mist is a perfect example of when it's done well.

    While the game's roster of bosses is quite varied, its developers understand the magic of fighting a humanoid adversary who, true to FromSoftware's philosophy, forces you to decipher a rapid and relentless attack pattern where the slightest mistake is punished with death.

    Gilroy is a challenge that evolves in each of the three encounters, always leaving room for more secrets, until the final confrontation arrives with the full weight of the narrative, where you must fight one last battle that is as bittersweet as it is satisfying.

    Ender Magnolia is a game that relies heavily on its aesthetics, story, and music to amplify its emotional impact, so the campaign reaches its peak when you must defeat this recurring and memorable figure one last time.

    Speaking of recurring tropes throughout video game history, Tunic presents The Heir as the final boss very early in the story, allowing you to become familiar with its power while simultaneously understanding how far you are from completing your journey.

    Games with such a strong emphasis on exploration and adventure as this one must make every element contribute to the sense of progress, and nothing demonstrates your growth more than a superpowered entity with whom you gradually close the gap.

    Checking your evolution through repeated attempts over many hours is captivating, as is finally realizing you're on par and understanding the remarkable challenge it truly holds, hidden behind complex and rapid combos, diverse area attacks, and far more resistance than you initially expected.

    The Heir's fight is simple but makes the most of Tunic's functional mechanics, and the satisfaction of delivering the final blow after so many hours lost and disoriented is unparalleled.

    Ori and the Will of the Wisps constantly surpasses itself with each upcoming boss, escape sequence, and scene, culminating in a Shriek encounter that ranges from breathtaking to utterly devastating.

    The franchise is a relentless litany of tragedies and victims that exact a toll on the kindness of those who suffer them, leading you to confront a majestic yet deeply traumatized owl amidst what appears to be the end of the universe.

    The screen seems to crumble as your confrontation with Shriek unfolds dynamically, with both combat and platforming sections taking place as the boss moves in and out of the frame with truly enviable dynamism.

    More than just a boss fight, the sequence feels like a genuine battle where a force of nature truly wants to defeat you; sensations enhanced by the magnificent soundtrack and the sheer madness of particles and colors displayed during the fight.

    Fighting Vahram in his godlike form inside the borders of time itself is among those images that stay with you forever, something Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown does quite regularly.

    These former brothers-in-arms clash in a magnificent duel where time freezes and reverses, beams of light and swords appear from all sides, and your adversary manipulates the laws of physics as if they were clay, making it a truly spectacular show.

    As you whittle down his health and he becomes cornered, the fight's complexity increases considerably, building to a tremendous crescendo where you feel the climax approaching and the adrenaline surging.

    Vahram is one of those bosses who can destroy you dozens of times in a row and you'll still be happy, because he's so well and precisely designed that each new opportunity to fight him again feels like a gift.

    True final bosses are usually the ultimate display of difficulty, depth, and passion that a Metroidvania has to offer, including Shii in MIO: Memories in Orbit.

    Fighting the companion who guided you throughout the story not because of some villainous adversity, but because of a genuine conflict of beliefs about what constitutes the most desirable outcome, is heartbreaking yet captivating, especially given the challenge that awaits.

    Shii lives up to his title, offering a multi-layered duel that demands you be as adept at recognizing openings as you are at dodging, jumping, dashing, grappling, flying, and more to evade its endless array of varied and omnidirectional attacks.

    The boss also flies, vanishes, glides, and crawls in an organic clash that makes the most of MIO: Memories in Orbit's environment and mechanics, resulting in an absolute delight.

    Blasphemous 2 boasts one of the most fluid and satisfying combat systems in the entire genre, but none exploit its flow state's sweet satisfaction quite like Eviterno, Last Desecrator.

    While the rest of the game is relatively manageable, this timeless warrior subverts expectations and delivers the beating of your life, proving that all the challenges you've overcome so far were just the tip of the iceberg he embodies.

    Far from the abominations and colossi you face during your crusade, the title presents, in its climax, a knight equal to you whose speed, power, and versatility demand pixel-perfect decision-making every second, regardless of your build.

    The best bosses are the ones that push you to your limits, and considering Eviterno penalizes even a millisecond off-timing or being a pixel too close, he's a clear contender for the decade's finest.

    Eigong is a mentor to our protagonist in Nine Sols both in story and gameplay, as no other encounter teaches you to appreciate its prodigious combat system so profoundly.

    There are fierce contenders throughout the campaign, though the one tasked with opposing Yi at the very end exponentially raises the demands of mechanical control, as any performance less than perfect will result in the same outcome: a return to the checkpoint.

    With three hellish phases brimming with rapid and agile movements—horizontal and vertical, parryable and unparryable, close and long range—it's an unstoppable barrage of abilities unless you know Yi's powers like the back of your hand.

    Only absolute, unwavering concentration will give you a chance against Eigong, whose defeat swiftly transforms from a painful climb into one of the most magical memories a Metroidvania has ever offered.

    Being the only one on the entire list who isn't the game's final boss, which already hints at her unparalleled quality, Skarrsinger Karmelita is Hollow Knight: Silksong's highest point.

    That Team Cherry's masterpiece has the genre's best boss this decade is undeniable, with representatives like Trobbio, Second Sentinel, Cogwork Dancers, and Lace to justify it, but ultimately it's the queen of the ants who gets the recognition.

    It's a majestic encounter from the very beginning, leading you through the halls of a theater with her glorious singing, and then, after gifting you her minions as an offering to start the fight with full silk, appearing on stage to give you the concert of your life.

    It has been revealed that the song, setting, art direction, attacks, rhythm, duration... Everything is perfectly timed to ensure a flawless experience, whether it takes you one try or a thousand (which is more likely).

    Skarrsinger Karmelita, I dare say, is among the best bosses in video game history and a perfect example of why this gameplay concept has gained so much relevance over the years.

    GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing.
    • But my newly introduced favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.
    • According to recent reports, GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me.

    But my newly introduced favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.

    According to recent reports, GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff.

    Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite upcoming features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles: When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point.

    Recent findings suggest that I've been calling this low-speed mode. At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode.

    It has been revealed that don't worry, it's not hard to fully gun it either: Just pull the trigger with a little gusto and you're off to the races. This is what the two speeds look like:.

    This has completely changed how I drive in GTA. I'm already someone who takes these games slowly, but the natural stopping point of the throttle makes this easy and natural—as if Rockstar is not just allowing for a more immersive playstyle, but endorsing it.

    Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

    It's just a different experience than having to manually learn the speed thresholds and intuitively hold the trigger at an exact middle point. This is more like I'm pulling the trigger to one natural stop for "slow", and another for "fast". It's the four-wheeled equivalent of Jason and Lucia's walk (you have to press L3 to enter a jog or sprint), or the default saunter of Red Dead Redemption 2's horses.

    According to recent reports, I can only recall one other open world game with a similar feature: the older Mafia games had speed limit toggles that automatically prevented cars from surpassing the speed limit. I always liked that, too, but this is more elegant.

    In a recent development, it turns out Rockstar's co-branding campaign that insists GTA 6 "plays best on PS5" isn't just marketing. In these months before GTA 6 is a PC game, I really would suggest you play it on a PlayStation for the controller perks alone. And when the time comes, I hope Rockstar goes the extra mile to port these DualSense features to the PC version.

    • Recent findings suggest that you know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022.
    • This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled.
    • Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that you know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

    This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony remarked that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring fresh creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

    Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

    Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

    Industry observers note that for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vg247 ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

    📅 06 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (398 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next massive game has officially released.
    • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.
    • Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next massive game has officially released. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

    The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

    Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

    According to recent reports, the open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

    According to recent reports, in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

    According to recent reports, marathon has now officially introduced, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

    Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

    Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game presently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

    It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After the Clean Up After Donnie GTA 6 mission, Donnie becomes a fence you can sell narcotics, marked notes, and jewelry to, all you have to do is drop them in the deposit box at his trailer in Key Lento. But with Brian also a fence, you may be wondering whether it's more beneficial to sell your goods to Donnie or Brian. While one may offer more lucrative rewards, all that glitters isn't necessarily gold in GTA 6.

    Sources indicate that if you hover your cursor over a fencing location icon on the GTA 6 map, you can see the rate each respective fence is offering for narcotics, marked bills, and jewelry. In GTA 6 Chapter 1, Donnie (Donnie's Trailer) pays low for narcotics, and very low for jewelry and marked bills.

    Brian (Brian's Lockup), on the other hand, pays very low for all three types of illicit products. As such, Donnie pays more than Brian for narcotics. For example, if you collect all the cocaine drops Cal tells you about after the Clean Up After Donnie mission and fence them, Donnie offers you $3,400, while Brian offers just $2,720. Do note that the time it takes for these payments to reach your mailbox can be impacted by any available missions.

    Recent findings suggest that while Donnie pays more, Cal suggests you sell the cocaine drops you collect to Brian, by depositing them at Brian's Lockup in Key Lento. He doesn't say why, but he seems to know something you don't. You should listen to Cal and sell your goods to Brian as the events of a later mission, called Swamped, might impact any payments Donnie owes you in GTA 6 (be aware of major spoilers by following that link).

    Note that if you sell to Brian and he seems to be taking his time to pay you, there may be an available Brian mission you must complete before your payment is sent to the mailbox at Jason's House.

    #97840. Industry News: Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

    📅 10 Mar 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (509 w)
    📖 Baca

    Industry News: Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

    📅 10 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
    • Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
    • According to recent reports, to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

    Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

    According to recent reports, to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

    According to recent reports, the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

    In a recent development, the amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

    While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

    Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

    In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

    You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

    Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

    Sources indicate that there’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

    You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

    #97838. Breaking: 10 Best N64 Racing Games That Still Hold Up Today

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1720 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: 10 Best N64 Racing Games That Still Hold Up Today

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Let's just get something out of the way rapidly – you don't necessarily have to be great at a genre of games to enjoy playing them.
    • Most of the time I spent with racing games was on older consoles, most especially the Nintendo 64.
    • There's a lot of great games here, and so to avoid unnecessary bias, I've ranked them in large part based on their review score aggregates.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let's just get something out of the way rapidly – you don't necessarily have to be great at a genre of games to enjoy playing them. I mean, sure, I'm quite good at platformers and deckbuilders, and play a ton of those. But if I just stuck with them, I'd get bored eventually. Which is why I enjoy genres I'm not particularly good at, like racing games.

    Most of the time I spent with racing games was on older consoles, most especially the Nintendo 64. I clocked tons and tons of hours in many of them back then, and not just the most generic car racing games. I also played snowboarding games, water sports and even futuristic race car rallies. And honestly, every game on this N64 list still holds up today.

    There's a lot of great games here, and so to avoid unnecessary bias, I've ranked them in large part based on their review score aggregates. Though in some cases, I did shuffle the order a bit when common sense called for it. So get ready, get set, and let's go through some epic N64 racing games!

    Nintendo doesn't always have the most luck with launch titles, at least when they're not heavy hitters like Mario or Zelda. Which is why I was so delighted with Pilotwings 64 heralding the new console. It was very stylish, and built on the previous SNES adventure in great ways.

    It has been revealed that your goal is to prove your stuff to earn a variety of pilot licenses in the game, and you'll have to accomplish some challenging feats. Those include autogyro, jet pack and hang gliding, even a human cannonball. Feats that aren't for the timid.

    Even though the game is graphically less impressive today, the core gameplay still holds up, and offers a robust challenge and plenty of bonus activities for players. And thanks to the hard work Paradigm put in researching military vehicles and flight sims, Pilotwings 64 is just as relevant today as it was back then.

    It shows the breadth of the racing game library on the N64 when the first futuristic racer isn't F-Zero X, but instead is Extreme-G. Which isn't a dig, mind you, since both games offered a lot. But for this particular adventure, the highlights were some really epic weapons like homing missiles and laser mines, as well as really innovative, gravity defying courses.

    Industry observers note that the game also featured frenetic deathmatches, which made sense on paper, but in execution were a bit muddled. Sure, there's the likes of capture the flag, competitive racing and battle mode, but they were less fun than they were stress inducing.

    It has been revealed that the biggest reason Extreme-G isn't ranked higher on this list is likely due to the graphics, which were fine but not overly impressive or creative. Still, if you had a need for speed and didn't mind using powerful weapons, this was a thrilling adventure.

    It has been revealed that while your mileage with arcade machines may vary, generally speaking they're massive, bold and visually impressive. And that goes double for racing games like San Francisco Rush 2049. Thankfully, they ported it to the N64, and brought high-octane energy to Nintendo's console.

    It has been revealed that what was most impressive about this adventure on consoles is that you could extend wings from your vehicles and glide in mid-air. You'll mostly use that in the stunt mode to rack up crazy points as you do complex maneuvers.

    Best of all, you had a lot to unlock in San Francisco Rush 2049, including new cars and tracks. Meaning that even now, this is a racing game you'll be spending a lot of time playing on the Nintendo 64 and even PC.

    Since the developer of the Wipeout series was owned by Sony Computer Entertainment, it makes sense most of the games weren't on Nintendo consoles. The one exception was Wipeout 64. While perhaps not a true sequel to Wipeout 2097, this standalone Nintendo adventure offered a lot to enjoy.

    In a recent development, perhaps the most impressive way Wipeout 64 differentiated itself from the others in the series was a split screen allowing up to 4 players to play together. Even with that aside, the game offered robust anti-gravity racing and truly superior track design.

    Recent findings suggest that if you enjoy racers with a variety of weapons, great tracks and a variety of gameplay modes, this N64 game had you covered. That said, perhaps the graphics were a step down from some of the other entries, but this was still a remarkably fun game.

    Much as I love Nintendo, sometimes you have to wait a long while between sequels. Zelda fans know what I'm talking about, but even they didn't have to wait as long for a sequel as fans of the original Excitebike on the NES. 16 years later, it got its first sequel in Excitebike 64.

    Sources indicate that as you might expect, the jump from 2D to 3D was a substantial one, and you're capable of epic tricks in Excitebike 64. Brake, slide, turbo boost and even tilt the bike in midair, there's a lot of options. Better yet, the various playable athletes have distinct stats, allowing players to pick the one that works best with their style.

    My favorite aspect of the game is playing through the extensive season mode, unlocking upcoming content along the way. But the one part of the game that really sets it apart is using the track editor to make your own insane obstacle courses.

    Sources indicate that racing games on Nintendo consoles often lean into the fantastical, patterning themselves after the likes of Mario Kart. But one that really took a major swing was Diddy Kong Racing. Not only did it feature different vehicles ranging from car to hovercraft to aeroplane, but there were also several different drivers and even a story involving the nefarious Wizpig.

    Like any of the Donkey Kong games, there's a lot of unlockables here, including obtaining amulet pieces to battle the true final boss. And if that wasn't enough, you'll even deal with actual boss battles of sorts, and use balloons to gain a huge variety of powerups, ranging from missiles to speed boosts and shields.

    According to recent reports, best of all, Diddy Kong Racing was quite pretty for the time, and the graphical style still looks great years later. Sure, it could get a bit repetitive, but this was still a really outstanding game you'd need to play on Nintendo 64.

    Sources indicate that I mentioned earlier that I'm not the best at racing games, but I'm especially bad when they're on water. Which perhaps makes Wave Race 64 especially intimidating. That said, if you put in enough practice time, even a rookie at the genre would find themselves loving this innovative and stunt-filled racing adventure.

    Sources indicate that playing against the clock while trying to steer your way around buoys and avoid the hazing of your opponent could be really tough. If you're skilled, you'll power up and go even faster, but if you fail, you'll get way behind. Thankfully, though, this is a quite attractive N64 game which is even better when racing against a friend.

    It has been revealed that if you're more skilled at racing than me, you'll probably adore Wave Race 64. It's the sort of retro that still holds up today, and it offers a phenomenally fun time, assuming you can react quickly to the choppy waters.

    Even though I never played any skateboarding games, I really adored Snowboard Kids. I'm not sure what it was about this N64 adventure, but it hooked me hard. Maybe it was the cute, cartoony graphics, or the simple yet well balanced gameplay. But this was one of those games I found myself playing again and again.

    The simple hook of the game is doing tricks while airborne to get coins, and then using them to buy powerups on tracks. You can have active and support items, such as hurling rocks at your opponents or turning temporarily invisible.

    In a recent development, perhaps the most surprising aspect of Snowboard Kids was that it was published by Atlus, who are usually known for JRPGs. But this is just one of those games that is still a ton of fun today, which I can attest to having played it recently with my close friends on their N64.

    Even though I'm not amazing at racing games, I spent many, many hours playing Mario Kart 64. I barely touched Super Mario Kart, didn't do much with the later entries, but that N64 game was one I kept returning to with friends.

    Recent findings suggest that there was just something about this game that made it one of the most iconic entries in the longrunning series. Maybe it was the quirky cast of Mario characters, maybe it was tracks like Rainbow Road. But this was a truly fun racing game that appealed to players of various abilities.

    Mix in various engine classes, a wide class of racers and amazingly fun attack items, and you have a great game in Mario Kart 64. But if that wasn't enough, it also features some of the best courses in the series, complete with really catchy tunes.

    According to recent reports, if you have a need for speed, you need look no further than F-Zero X. This futuristic series featured some of the most blisteringly fast courses and crazy racers you'll see in any series. And honestly, F-Zero X is still probably one of the best racers ever. So even though it's shameful we haven't gotten a sequel, you might not need it either.

    Sources indicate that death Race offered a truly unhinged way to play the game, and the randomness of X-Cup could keep you playing the game for a long time. So even though it's not the most graphically impressive game, the high framerate and fantasically weird drivers made this a worthy contender.

    Plasma Powered hovercars turned made racing even more fun, and so long as you can keep up, you'll find one of the best racers ever in F-Zero X. Here's hoping it gets an even better followup on modern consoles one day.
